backlog.spec: Add a `maxiter` argument to _solve_once and pass it into the SLSQP options. Fresh random starts keep MAX_ITER = 200. Perturbed starts in the perturbation phase use maxiter = 100, because they begin close to a good packing and need fewer iterations. This gives roughly twice as many perturbation trials in the same time. Change nothing else: same sd choices, same 0.5 radius shrink, same repair and acceptance rule.
backlog.title: Fewer SLSQP iterations for perturbed starts

backlog.spec: For half of the fresh random starts, set initial radii so that 10 random circles have radius 0.08 and the other 16 have radius 0.035, with uniform random centres in [0.1,0.9]. The other half stay as the current start. Tests heterogeneous starting radii that match the structure of good packings.
backlog.title: Two-radius-class starts

backlog.spec: In solve, change the perturbation sd choices from [0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05] to [0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.03]. This concentrates the search closer to the best basin. Keep the 30% restart phase, radii x0.5 and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Smaller perturbation sd pool

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, maintain a Gaussian centre-jitter sd starting at 0.02. After each child, if its radius sum beats the best, multiply sd by 1.5. If it does not, multiply sd by 0.97. Keep sd within [0.002, 0.1]. Build each child by jittering the best centres with the current sd and halving the radii, then run SLSQP and _repair. Keep the restart phase as in slot 2. This is the classical one-fifth success rule applied to the existing perturbation step, instead of a fixed choice of sd.
backlog.title: Adaptive jitter scale from the one-fifth success rule

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 8% of the time limit. Take the best packing and run SLSQP from its centres and radii (not scaled) with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter 300, using the same constraints. Repair, and keep the result only if its repaired sum is larger than the best's. Restart/perturbation loop ends at 0.72 of the time limit.
backlog.title: Final polish with tight-tolerance SLSQP

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts in _solve_once, replace the constant INIT_RADIUS with radii that make the start feasible: after drawing centres c of shape (n, 2), compute the pairwise distance matrix with the diagonal set to inf, then r0 = 0.45 * minimum(nearest-neighbour distance, distance to the nearest wall) per circle, where the wall distance is min(x, y, 1 - x, 1 - y). Use x0 = concatenate([c.ravel(), r0]). Every constraint is then satisfied at the start, so SLSQP starts from a feasible point instead of resolving overlaps first. Perturbed starts are unchanged.
backlog.title: Feasible clearance-based initial radii for fresh starts

backlog.spec: After 30% of the time limit, keep a current packing (initially best). Each iteration perturb the current packing (radii x0.5, centre noise sd chosen from [0.005,0.01,0.02]), re-optimise with SLSQP, repair. Accept as current if its sum is >= current sum minus 0.002; update best separately. This chains perturbations instead of always restarting from the best. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Chained perturb-and-accept from current packing

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, half the time (rng.random() < 0.5), transform the best centres before the usual jitter: c' = 0.5 + (c - 0.5) * [1 + e, 1 - e] with e ~ U(-0.06, 0.06). This stretches the packing along one axis and squeezes it along the other. Clip to [0.02, 0.98], add normal jitter with sd 0.005, use radii x0.5 and run SLSQP. The other half of the time, use the existing perturbation.
backlog.title: Global anisotropic stretch perturbation

backlog.spec: Pass options={'maxiter': MAX_ITER, 'ftol': 1e-10} to minimize when _solve_once is called with a start (the perturbation phase). Fresh random restarts keep the default ftol. Local optima found near the best packing then converge fully instead of stopping about 1e-6 short. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Tighter SLSQP ftol on perturbation runs

backlog.spec: Split the usable time (TIME_FRACTION * time_limit) into 3 equal episodes. Each episode has its own local best, starting from None: for the first 30% of the episode run fresh random restarts, then perturb the episode best for the rest of the episode, exactly as the current loop does. Keep a global best over all episodes and return it. Implement it as an outer `for k in range(3)` loop with episode start and end times computed from t0; the inner loop is the current loop body with the episode clock. The aim is to reduce the variance that comes from a single perturbation chain being stuck in a poor basin.
backlog.title: Three independent restart-then-perturb episodes

backlog.spec: Rescale the decision vector so that all variables are of similar magnitude. Optimise y = (centres, 10*radii) instead of (centres, radii), so the radius variables are O(1) like the coordinates. Inside _solve_once, convert x0 by multiplying the radii by 10, and convert the result back by dividing by 10 before returning. The objective is -sum(y[2n:])/10 and the constraints are unchanged in form, with the radius references multiplied by 10. This tests whether SLSQP's step and line-search behaviour improves with better-scaled variables, with no other change.
backlog.title: SLSQP variable rescaling for conditioning

backlog.spec: Build a fresh start by placing circles one at a time. For each new circle, sample 400 candidate points uniformly in the square with rng, and choose the one with the largest clearance, meaning the minimum of distance to existing centres minus existing radii and distance to the walls. Set that circle's initial radius to the clearance capped at 0.15. Use the resulting centres and radii as x0 for SLSQP. Use this start for about half of the fresh restarts and keep uniform starts for the rest.
backlog.title: Greedy max-clearance sequential placement start

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, with probability 0.4 apply a squeeze move to the best packing: pick a random axis, scale the centres' coordinate on that axis about 0.5 by a factor 0.9, then add noise sd 0.01 and halve the radii and re-optimise. Other times use the existing jitter. This opens up gaps at the walls for rearrangement.
backlog.title: Squeeze wall perturbation

backlog.spec: Maintain a population of 8 packings from the restart phase, each stored as (centres, radii). For each generation, form a child for each member with a DE/rand/1 move on the centres: child = a + 0.6*(b - c), applied coordinate-wise with crossover rate 0.9 against the parent, clipped to [0.05, 0.95]. Run the existing SLSQP from the child centres with radii set to 0.5 times the parent radii, then _repair. Replace the parent if the child's radius sum is larger. Use this loop for the final 50% of the time, and return the best member. Keep the code to one generation function.
backlog.title: Memetic differential-evolution over centre sets

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, change the bounds on the radius variables so that each radius is at least R_MIN = 0.01 during the SLSQP run. Implement this with the constraint r_i - R_MIN >= 0 instead of the existing r_i >= 0, which is already in cons, or by passing a bounds argument to minimize with method SLSQP. This keeps circles from collapsing to zero size and wasting degrees of freedom, so the optimiser has to find a packing in which every circle is usable. The repair step is unchanged, and the floor is only used inside SLSQP.
backlog.title: Minimum radius floor during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Change SHRINK from 1e-9 to 2e-11 and verify inside _repair after shrinking that the max pairwise overlap and wall violation are <= 0; if any violation remains, subtract a further 1e-11 from the offending radii in a loop up to 5 times. This keeps the packing valid under the 1e-10 tolerance while gaining a tiny amount of radius sum.
backlog.title: Tighter repair shrink

backlog.spec: For each fresh random start, run a first SLSQP stage (60 iterations) with objective -sum(w*r) where w is random per circle in [0.5,1.5], then run the normal unweighted objective for 200 iterations from that result. Fresh starts only. Weights break symmetry and give diverse size distributions.
backlog.title: Weighted-objective annealed warm start

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, choose the centre-noise sd by elapsed fraction: it starts at 0.04 right after the restart phase and decays linearly to 0.005 at the end of the time. Radii still x0.5 as now. Replaces the random choice of [0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05].
backlog.title: Perturb size schedule decaying over time

backlog.spec: During the fresh-restart phase (first 30% of the time) keep the two best packings instead of one. From 30% to 55% of the time, alternate perturbation trials between the two, each chain perturbing and updating its own best with the current sd choices and 0.5 radius shrink. At 55% of the time, drop the chain with the lower sum of radii and spend the remaining time perturbing only the winner as now. Return the overall best. If only one packing exists at 30%, run the single chain as now. There is no recombination between the chains.
backlog.title: Two-chain tournament before committing to one packing

backlog.spec: Add a maxiter argument to _solve_once with default MAX_ITER. Fresh random restarts keep 200 iterations. Perturbation runs, which start near a good optimum, use maxiter=100, so more perturbation trials fit in the time. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Shorter SLSQP for perturbation runs

memo: Helped: only slot 2 (30% of time on random restarts, then perturb the best packing with radii x0.5 and re-optimise), -2.6349, one run, unconfirmed given noise sd 0.0023. Slot 29 (remove 3 smallest circles and reinsert) gave the best raw value, -2.6360, but was rejected against the incumbent's adjusted measure. Slots 6, 7, 16, 18 and 27 reached -2.6354, within noise of slot 2. Did not help: LP radii, swaps, relocating small circles (-2.6249), analytic Jacobians, screening, wall-biased, Latin hypercube, mirrored and random-radii starts, higher time fraction, basin hopping, pruning, long final polish, crossover, rotate/translate (-2.6275). Start-distribution and solver changes mostly hurt. Next: replicate slots 2, 16 and 29 to confirm the -2.635 level, since single runs are noisy. Tune the restart fraction (20% vs 50%) and perturbation size. Try repeated perturb-and-reoptimise cycles. Combine slot 29 with slot 6 or 7 starts. Avoid already-tried ideas (several were aborted as duplicates).
